fred-us-retail-sales-2026-08-14.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly estimate of receipts at US retail and food-service businesses, released around the middle of the following month. It is the earliest broad read on consumer spending, which drives roughly two-thirds of the US economy.

ecb-2026-09.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets policy rates for the euro area on a roughly six-week cycle. Its decisions set the cost of credit across twenty member economies and anchor the euro against every currency it trades with.

fomc-2026-09.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight bank lending. Its decisions move borrowing costs across the dollar economy and price every asset quoted against the dollar.
fomc-2026-09.recent: The committee meets with the dollar at its weakest since May and gold near $4,392 an ounce, and with Trump moving a second time to fire Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence. The Bank of England held at 3.75% with three of nine dissenting and the Bank of Japan held at 1%, leaving the Fed the outlier still to decide.

boe-2026-09.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its decisions set the cost of borrowing across the UK economy, feeding into mortgages, sterling and gilt yields.
boe-2026-09.recent: The committee meets after a run of holds elsewhere: the Bank of Japan kept rates at 1% while warning underlying inflation is exceeding its 2% target, and the RBA held steady as its housing market softened. In the UK, house prices rose 0.1% in July as buyers stayed cautious on interest rates.

boj-2026-09.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board sets the short-term interest rate roughly eight times a year. Its decisions set the price of the world's cheapest funding currency, and move the yen, Japanese government bonds and carry trades built on them.
boj-2026-09.recent: The board held at 1% on July 31 while warning that underlying inflation is exceeding its 2% target, and Tokyo sold dollars for yen hours earlier. Washington then joined a historic joint intervention on August 3. A weak yen has been lifting exporters, with Toyota's quarterly profit reaching $9.4 billion.

uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The UK's monthly consumer price index, published by the Office for National Statistics, measuring how much prices paid by households have changed over the past year. It is the reference number for Bank of England rate decisions, index-linked gilts, and a range of benefits and rail fares.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The release lands as inflation data drives markets elsewhere: India's retail inflation rose to 4.45% in July from 4.38% in June on food prices, and crypto traders moved around US CPI day, with bitcoin near $63,500. This print will set the annual UK rate the Bank of England weighs at its next meeting.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight bank lending. Its decisions move the cost of borrowing across the dollar economy, and with it assets priced against the dollar.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The committee meets with its own composition in dispute: Trump is trying again to fire Cook, reviving the Fed independence fight. The dollar has already fallen to its weakest since May with a rate hike in doubt, gold hit $4,392 an ounce, and other central banks have split — three of nine BoE policymakers voted to raise.

ecb-2026-10.recent: The decision lands after a stretch in which the other major central banks have chosen to wait: the Bank of Japan held at 1% while warning that underlying inflation is exceeding its 2% target, and the RBA held steady as its housing market softened. The dollar has fallen to its lowest level since May.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate. Its decisions set the price of the world's cheapest funding currency, and move the yen, Japanese government bonds and global carry trades.

Tokyo sold dollars for yen around that decision, and on August 3 the US joined a joint intervention that pushed the dollar to a one-month low. The gap between the rate and the currency is what this meeting has to close.
